nodes.question: In the edited image, is the same blue-covered book from the source visibly behind the same rose from the source, with the rose in front, as shown by relative depth or occlusion?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the source book and source rose are identifiable and visible evidence establishes the book behind that rose. Fail if the identifiable objects clearly are not in that relation. Unknown if object identity or their relative depth cannot be determined; do not assume changed-looking objects are replacements.
nodes.binding: Compare the edited image with the source image to identify the blue-covered book and rose, then assess only their requested behind/in-front relation using visible placement and occlusion cues. Occlusion is strong evidence but is not mandatory if other clear depth cues establish the relation.

nodes.question: Does the edited image show genuine progress toward placing the same source book behind the same source rose, even if the requested placement is incomplete?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if identifiable source objects show a changed relative placement or other clear visual evidence of movement toward the book-behind-rose relation, without establishing complete fulfillment. Fail if the identifiable objects clearly show no such progress. Unknown if identity or progress cannot be determined. Changes to object appearance or unrelated objects alone are not progress.
nodes.binding: Compare source and edited images to track the source blue-covered book and rose. Judge progress toward their requested depth relation, not merely whether either object changed; use visible relative placement and depth cues, without requiring overlap when other clear evidence supports progress.

nodes.question: Is the book visibly positioned behind the flower?
nodes.criteria: Apply the original rubric to R1 using both supports. Complete (yes) only if s1 passes. Partial only if s2 passes and s1 does not pass. Absent (no) only if both supports fail and their evidence establishes that the identifiable source objects show no requested progress. Unknown if either support is unknown, or if failures do not establish absence of progress. Do not count unrelated edits as progress; never infer a visual failure from transport failure or missing evidence.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The binding is truncated/ambiguous (“visibly (...)”) and should explicitly preserve the requested source-object relation: the source book behind the source flower, judged by relative depth/occlusion in the edited image. Keep identity matching separate from placement: the edit shows a blue book and two yellow flowers, while the source has a blue book and a red-yellow rose; do not treat flower substitution alone as proof of placement failure, but require evidence that the relevant source objects can be matched and assess any visible progress. The repeated traces mostly support no progress because the book appears separate from the flowers, but one valid unknown trace arises when the rose cannot be identified. Preserve that uncertainty rather than converting it to absent; the aggregate’s unresolved case is not a transport failure (dependencies were queried and valid), whereas the empty execution reference/invalid parent result is a schema/execution issue and should not be interpreted as visual evidence. Clarify the node’s evidence and routing criteria so unknown identity or insufficient depth evidence remains unresolved, while absent requires affirmative visual evidence of no requested progress; do not let high confidence or repeated runs substitute for that evidence.
s2: The binding is truncated and should explicitly anchor the decision to the same source book and rose and their relative depth, while keeping object identity separate from placement. In these images the book has changed orientation/position and the rose appears replaced by two yellow flowers; neither appearance change nor substitution alone establishes progress. Assess whether the source objects can be matched and whether visible relative-position or occlusion cues show movement toward book-behind-rose. Fail only when identifiable objects affirmatively show no such progress; retain unknown when identity or depth evidence is insufficient. The unresolved trace is valid visual uncertainty, not a transport failure; keep schema/execution errors separate from visual evidence, and do not use repeated high-confidence fails to override uncertainty.
s1: Repair the truncated binding and make the decision explicitly compare the source book and source rose with the edited image, separating identity matching from the requested depth relation. Judge progress only from visible evidence that the matched book is moving behind the matched rose; changed orientation or flower appearance alone neither proves nor disproves progress. In this edit the blue book and two yellow flowers are visible, but the source rose is not clearly identifiable and the book appears separate from them: treat that as unresolved if identity/depth cannot be established, and call no progress only when affirmative visual evidence supports it. Keep valid visual uncertainty distinct from transport/schema failures; repeated high-confidence runs do not resolve ambiguous identity.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The fulfillment rule can misclassify unresolved evidence as absent: it says “Absent (no) if both checks fail” without requiring that the checks establish no requested progress across the relevant evidence. In particular, s1 can fail because the book is not fully behind a flower while s2 fails because progress is not established; those failures do not necessarily prove no progress. The rubric requires insufficient evidence to remain unresolved, so the readout must not treat these failures as sufficient evidence for no.

findings.question: Does the edited image show the source book behind the source rose, with the rose in front, or otherwise show clear progress toward that relative-depth arrangement?
findings.criteria: Compare the identifiable source book and rose across both images. Assess their relative depth and occlusion; do not treat changed flower appearance or the book's changed position alone as progress. If the source rose cannot be identified or the depth relation is unclear, report unknown rather than fail.
findings.evidence: The source shows a blue-covered book and a single red-and-yellow rose. The edited image shows a blue-covered book and two small yellow flowers; the book appears separate from both, with no visible overlap establishing the requested depth order.
findings.rationale: The saved checks repeatedly claim the rose is replaced or unidentifiable, while some also claim both source objects are identifiable. A focused visual check of identity and the book–rose depth relation would resolve this inconsistency and guard against both overclaiming completion and treating uncertain identity as proof of no progress.
